criteria.reasoning: The memo reports Marwood's "Total Grants Paid: $708,000 across 10 grants," and its summary table repeats $708,000. It does not use the $804,400 total-disbursements figure.

The memo states that Marwood's Form 990-PF "checks the box stating that the foundation 'only makes contributions to preselected charitable organizations and does not accept unsolicited requests for funds'." It also quotes the website: "does not accept unsolicited proposals, letters of inquiry or applications."

The memo says Marwood "may receive no unsolicited proposal, letter of inquiry, application, or other written request for funds" and "Staff prepare no materials." A proposal is sent only "If Marwood issues a written invitation." Briefing Lindqvist herself is the only step before an invitation.

The memo identifies "Margaret W. Lindqvist, a Director on Millstream's Board of Directors, serves as a Trustee ... of the Marwood Family Foundation." It recommends that she "approach fellow Marwood trustees to ask whether the foundation would welcome a conversation with Millstream or invite a formal request."
The memo reports Calloway-Deane's "Total Grants Paid: $390,000 across 12 grants," not the $488,450 total-disbursements figure.

The memo states "0 of 12 grants. All 12 grants paid in 2025 went to organizations in North Carolina (5 grants), South Carolina (4 grants), and Virginia (3 grants)," and notes the Lancaster County Hunger Coalition grant is in "Lancaster, South Carolina." It finds geography "NOT A FIT" and says the Philadelphia trustee address does not establish fit.

The memo states "Millstream must not apply for the October 15, 2026 deadline." It allows only "a single phone ... or email inquiry" about Pennsylvania eligibility, with "no proposal or LOI" unless written confirmation is received.
The memo reports Garrison Ridge's "Total Grants Paid: $480,000 across 13 grants," which leaves out the grants approved for future payment.

The memo recommends "Submit an online LOI of up to two pages via Garrison Ridge's portal." It rates geography a "High fit" because the guidelines "explicitly list Lancaster County" and "12 of 13 grants paid in 2025 were to PA organizations."

The memo limits Garrison Ridge to "Program support only" because "All 13 grants paid in 2025 were for program or operating support," and the website says grants "support programs and the organizations that run them." It concludes Millstream "cannot request capital funding from Garrison Ridge, but may request program support for the southern-county mobile markets."
The memo notes that the fall LOIs closed September 1, 2026 and gives "Spring 2027 cycle: LOI due March 1, 2027 at 5:00 p.m. Eastern" as the next deadline.
The memo lists the seven comparable Pennsylvania food grants ($15,000 to $60,000), excludes Mason-Dixon (MD), and gives "Top of Range (Median - 4th grant): $30,000."
The memo recommends "Ask Range: $15,000 to $30,000" for Garrison Ridge program support.
The memo ranks "First Priority: Garrison Ridge Foundation," "Second Priority: Marwood Family Foundation," and "Third Priority: Calloway-Deane Charitable Trust."

The only board connection asserted is Lindqvist's Marwood trusteeship. For Calloway it says "Dr. Owen M. Calloway is a Millstream board director, but has no role with the Calloway-Deane Charitable Trust," and that he "suggested the trust solely because he read about its funding priorities." The grants, deadlines, phone and email contacts and policies attributed to each foundation all appear in the files.
